title: Northstar Health - integration call notes
content:
Meeting: Northstar Health - Redwood integration kick-off
Date: 2026-06-18
Attendees: Dr. Priya Menon (Northstar product), Liam O'Neill (Northstar netops), Samir Rao (Northstar security), Avery Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Redwood infra), Simone Alvarez (Redwood customer success)

Purpose: surface network/security requirements and high-level rollout plan for Private deployment (VPC + on-prem option) so Northstar can process PHI under HIPAA constraints.

Summary / outcomes:
- Northstar confirmed requirement to keep PHI inside their VPC (no egress of raw PHI to hosted multi-tenant services). They are evaluating Redwood Private (control plane with customer-managed network) or an on-prem package if needed.
- Primary integration target: conversational triage assistant + record summarization. Expected peak: ~120 concurrent sessions mornings (08:00-11:00 PST), baseline ~20 concurrent. Avg prompt length ~400 tokens, avg response 600 tokens.
- SLA target: 99.95% availability for the inference endpoints during business hours; recovery/MTTR expectations discussed (target < 15m for P1).
- Security: must support customer-managed KMS (HSM preferred), full audit logs, and SOC2/HIPAA artifacts.

Technical requirements / notes:
- Network: Northstar will do VPC peering/VPN to Redwood private nodes in GCP us-central1. Liam to confirm CIDR ranges and firewall rules. Need diagram for required ports and IPs from Redwood (Avery to deliver).
- Auth: customer prefers mTLS for service-to-service traffic + short-lived tokens from their identity provider (Okta). Redwood to confirm support for mTLS + token introspection flow.
- Data residency: all inference compute must execute in customer VPC; no model telemetry with PHI may leave VPC. Redwood discussed option: local logging & metrics export to customer collector (Splunk) and minimal aggregated telemetry to Redwood control plane excluding PHI.
- Models: Northstar wants to start with a smaller open model (7B quantized) for cost predictability, then evaluate 13B if quality deficits appear. We recommended enabling kv-cache/prefix caching for conversation flows to reduce latency and cost.
- Latency: target tail P95 < 800ms for single-turn summaries on the 7B config. For multi-turn triage flows, acceptable P95 up to 1.2s. Jordan suggested batching policy tuned to morning burst pattern; we should simulate traffic to produce guidance.
- Storage: embeddings for retrieval should be stored in customer's managed DB (they use Firestore-like managed DB). We need to validate connector and sample throughput.

Risk / gotchas identified:
- PHI in telemetry: ensure default logging scrubs/filters are excluded or routed only to customer collector. Action: clarify Redwood telemetry defaults and provide configuration option to disable PHI telemetry.
- Network egress: some secondary services (image OCR, NER) may call external APIs; Northstar prohibits external calls for PHI. Need to enumerate optional features that require outbound calls.
- Model size vs latency: 13B may fail latency SLO for peak unless we reserve Dedicated capacity. Discuss reserved Dedicated GPUs or pre-warmed private nodes for peak windows.
- Canary rollback: must provide a predictable fallback path to a smaller/older model and route policy. This was discussed as required for their clinical rollout.

Open questions (need answers before next meeting):
- Can Redwood present a clear config snippet showing how to: (1) disable telemetry sending of request/response bodies; (2) enable mTLS + token introspection? (Avery)
- Will the on-prem package support the same rollout/console features (canary, tracing) or will some features be degraded? (Jordan/R&D)
- Estimated cost model for 7B quantized private deployment under their load (baseline and peak). Need sample cost breakdown (tokens, reserved capacity). (Simone / Finance)
- Does Redwood support HSM integration for key rotation policies Northstar requires? (Security/infra)

Action items / owners / due dates:
- Avery: Send network diagram + required CIDR/IPs and ports for VPC peering (deliverable: network diagram doc) - due 2026-06-21.
- Liam (Northstar): Share internal firewall change window and confirmed CIDR ranges by 2026-06-20.
- Jordan: Run a short traffic simulation (script) modeling morning burst (120 concurrent, token distribution provided) and return expected P95 latencies and recommended batching settings - due 2026-06-24.
- Simone: Prepare cost estimate for 7B private deployment (baseline vs peak) + options for reserved capacity vs burstable - due 2026-06-25.
- Samir (Northstar): Validate KMS/HSM requirements and share HSM vendor details - due 2026-06-22.
- Avery/Jordan: Prepare a short config snippet (no-PHI telemetry + mTLS example) and place in CONF-1834 - due 2026-06-21.
- Schedule follow-up: 30-minute sync to review network & latency sims on 2026-06-25 10:00am PST. Jordan to send calendar invite.

Notes to self / reminders:
- When drafting network diagram, include both VPC-peering and VPN options and a fallback plan if peering is delayed.
- For cost estimate, include quantized model memory footprint, expected GPU type for Private nodes, and expected token costs for embedding vs generation.
- Look up previous health-customer playbook (CONF-1120) for HIPAA checklist to attach to CONF-1834.

Draft follow-up email outline (for sending after deliverables):
Hi Priya/Liam/Samir,
Thanks for the time today — attached are the items we discussed: network diagram, preliminary config snippets (mTLS + telemetry toggle), and timeline for next steps. Per action items: Avery will deliver network diagram by Mon 6/21; Jordan will run the latency sims and share results by 6/24; Simone will share cost estimates by 6/25. Look forward to the follow-up on 6/25 at 10am PST.
Best,
Avery

-- end of notes
